subject.title: improve(setup): keep WSL operations inside the app-owned directory

question: Should standalone SetupEngine intentionally adopt the new restrictive ASCII distro-name contract, or should the policy preserve every name that can be safely contained beneath the app-owned WSL directory?
rationale: The containment hardening is well motivated, but the exact allowlist is a compatibility and security-policy choice rather than a conclusion established by the tests.

options.title: Approve strict contract
options.body: Accept the 1–64 character ASCII allowlist, document it as the supported standalone SetupEngine contract, and require live upgrade-style proof before merge.

options.title: Preserve safe names
options.body: Narrow validation to reject path separators, rooted or traversal names, and other unsafe Windows path forms while retaining compatible non-ASCII or spaced names that remain immediate children.

options.title: Pause the change
options.body: Leave current behavior unchanged until maintainers define the supported custom distro-name and filesystem-race threat model.

recommendation.title: Approve strict contract
recommendation.body: Accept the 1–64 character ASCII allowlist, document it as the supported standalone SetupEngine contract, and require live upgrade-style proof before merge.

likelyOwner.reason: He is the best available repository-level routing candidate for the setup compatibility and security-policy choice, although SetupEngine-specific ownership could not be established confidently.
